input: This capital appraisal examines a proposal to install a solar array, and it brings together the principal financial figures that decision-makers will need in order to judge whether the investment is worthwhile. The installed cost of the array comes to $1596k, which represents a substantial upfront commitment of capital. Set against this outlay, the array is expected to deliver a net saving of $257k per year, and this saving is projected to continue for 12 years. Because money received in the future is worth less than money held today, the appraisal applies a discount rate of 6% in order to express the future savings in present-day terms. On this basis, the present value of the savings works out at $2155k. Subtracting the installed cost from this figure gives a net present value of $559k, which is positive and therefore points, on the face of it, towards an attractive investment. It must nevertheless be stressed that the savings underpinning the entire calculation are vendor and utility estimates, and that no saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation, so the figures should be treated as projections rather than as established facts.
target: The solar array returns a net present value of $559k at a discount rate of 6%. The installed cost is $1596k. Expected net saving is $257k per year for 12 years, and the present value of the savings is $2155k, which exceeds the installed cost by the amount of the net present value. The array is appraised as a capital purchase set against a stream of avoided electricity purchases. The discount rate converts each year's saving to its present value before the savings are summed; the net present value is what remains after the installed cost is set against that sum. The appraisal horizon is the period over which the vendor and utility figures are projected, and no saving beyond that horizon is credited to the array. The case rests on the saving figure, and the saving figure is an estimate. The savings are vendor and utility estimates; no saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation. A shortfall in the annual saving passes directly into the net present value: the appraisal holds no measured performance to set against the estimate. The decision the appraisal supports is conditional on the saving being achieved at close to the estimated level, and a measured saving from a comparable array, once one exists, replaces the estimate as the basis of the case.
